title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Gross Monthly Income Verification
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.1 (Gross Monthly Income Verification): Gross monthly income shall be determined using verified, reliable documentation including the applicant's latest 3 months' salary slips, latest EPF statements, or verified bank account statements showing regular salary crediting. Overtime, allowances, and commissions shall be averaged over a consecutive 6-month period.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: DSR Ceiling for Gross Monthly Income Below RM 3,000
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.2 (DSR Ceiling for Gross Monthly Income Below RM 3,000): For applicants with a verified gross monthly income of less than RM 3,000, the Debt Service Ratio (DSR) ceiling is strictly capped at 60%. Applications exceeding this 60% threshold shall not be approved under standard underwriting authority.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: DSR Ceiling for Gross Monthly Income RM 3,000 and Above
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.3 (DSR Ceiling for Gross Monthly Income RM 3,000 and Above): For applicants with a verified gross monthly income of RM 3,000 or greater, the maximum permissible DSR ceiling is set at 70%. Underwriters must ensure total monthly debt obligations remain strictly within this parameter.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Binding Nature of Projected DSR
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.4 (Binding Nature of Projected DSR): All DSR calculations must incorporate the prospective monthly commitment of the applied financing facility. The projected DSR after the facility is granted is binding and serves as the definitive determinant for ratio-based credit qualification.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Delinquency and Arrears Thresholds
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.5 (Delinquency and Arrears Thresholds): An applicant who currently maintains any credit facility with AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad or other reporting financial institutions that is 2 or more months in arrears shall be declined immediately without exception.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Minimum Net Disposable Income (NDI) Floor
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.1 (Minimum Net Disposable Income (NDI) Floor): The minimum Net Disposable Income (NDI) floor is established at a flat RM 1,500 after the proposed facility is drawn in full. NDI is defined as verified gross monthly income minus all statutory deductions and total projected monthly debt commitments.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Dependants and Uniform NDI Standard
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.2 (Dependants and Uniform NDI Standard): Under this Policy Version 1.0, applicant dependants are recorded for demographic recordkeeping only. The NDI floor applies as a flat baseline of RM 1,500 across all individual applicant categories, with no differential threshold applied based on the number of dependants.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: CTOS Prime Tier Assessment
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.1 (CTOS Prime Tier Assessment): Applicants presenting a CTOS credit score of 700 or above qualify for the Prime Tier, representing low credit risk. Such applications may be routed through automated decisioning pipelines and standard risk pricing matrices.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: CTOS Standard Tier Assessment
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.2 (CTOS Standard Tier Assessment): Applicants presenting a CTOS credit score between 650 and 699 are assigned to the Standard Pricing Tier, subject to standard underwriting verification and confirmation of stable repayment history across external credit bureau records.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Sub-650 CTOS Score Underwriting Referral
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.4 (Sub-650 CTOS Score Underwriting Referral): Any application with a CTOS score below 650 is disqualified from automated decisioning pathways. Such files must be referred to a Senior Underwriter for comprehensive manual assessment and holistic credit review.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Mandatory Exclusionary Credit Triggers
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.5 (Mandatory Exclusionary Credit Triggers): An active legal action, record of bankruptcy, winding-up order, or an active Agensi Kaunseling dan Pengurusan Kredit (AKPK) flag registered on CTOS or CCRIS represents an absolute decline trigger across all retail product categories.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Initial Credit Limit Multipliers
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.2 (Initial Credit Limit Multipliers): Initial credit limits for credit cards and unsecured lines are restricted by income tiers: the approved credit limit must not exceed 2 times gross monthly income for applicants earning below RM 5,000, and must not exceed 3 times gross monthly income for applicants earning RM 5,000 or more.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Machine Learning Model Input Safeguards
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.4 (Machine Learning Model Input Safeguards): In compliance with risk governance frameworks, an applicant's approved credit limit must never be utilized as an input feature in any automated credit scoring or risk estimation model.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: AEON Credit Card Line Tiers and Annual Fees
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.1 (AEON Credit Card Line Tiers and Annual Fees): The Company offers three principal Visa card tiers: AEON Classic Visa carries an annual fee of RM 0 (free for life); AEON Gold Visa carries an annual fee of RM 150, waived upon a minimum of 12 swipes per card anniversary year; AEON Platinum Visa carries an annual fee of RM 400, waived upon achieving RM 30,000 in total annual retail spending.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Tiered Credit Card Finance Charges
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.2 (Tiered Credit Card Finance Charges): Card finance charges are calculated on a tiered basis: 15.00% per annum for prompt payers who settle minimum dues on time for 12 consecutive months; 17.00% per annum for cardholders with standard settlement history; and 18.00% per annum for cardholders who incur 2 or more late payments over the preceding 12 months.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq) Framework
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.3 (Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq) Framework): Personal Financing-i operates under the Shariah contract of Tawarruq with fixed profit rates ranging from 6.88% to 14.88% per annum flat. Financing tenures range from 12 to 84 months, with eligible financing amounts spanning RM 3,000 to RM 150,000.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP) Ineligibility
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.4 (AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP) Ineligibility): Applicants actively enrolled in an AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP) are strictly ineligible for any new unsecured credit facilities, including credit cards and Personal Financing-i.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i Parameters
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.1 (Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i Parameters): Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i facilities offer a maximum financing margin of up to 90% of the vehicle cash price. Repayment tenures are permitted from a minimum of 12 months up to a maximum of 60 months.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Auto Hire Purchase-i and Product Financing Terms
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.2 (Auto Hire Purchase-i and Product Financing Terms): Auto Hire Purchase-i financing allows a margin of up to 90% with financing tenures extendable up to 108 months. Product (Objective) Financing covers designated consumer durable goods up to approved institutional merchant scheme limits.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: Customer Complaint Handling and Timelines
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 8.1 (Customer Complaint Handling and Timelines): All customer disputes and underwriting complaints lodged with the Company must be formally acknowledged in writing within 2 business days and investigated and resolved within 14 calendar days from receipt.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v1)
heading: External Dispute Resolution via OFS
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v1 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v1) | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 8.4 (External Dispute Resolution via OFS): If an underwriting complaint or billing grievance cannot be resolved satisfactorily within the stipulated internal resolution period, the complainant must be informed of their right to escalate the dispute to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS).

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Scope and Policy Objectives
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 1.0 (Scope and Policy Objectives): This Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) applies to all credit assessment and underwriting operations within AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad ('the Company'). Effective 1 January 2026, this policy supersedes Credit Underwriting Policy v1 (effective 1 January 2025). The lending products governed under this policy comprise unsecured revolving credit (AEON Classic Visa, AEON Gold Visa, AEON Platinum Visa credit cards), Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq), Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i, Auto Hire Purchase-i, and Product (Objective) Financing. All underwriting officers, automated decision engines, and delegated approval authorities must adhere strictly to the standards defined herein.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Debt Service Ratio (DSR) Framework
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 2.0 (Debt Service Ratio (DSR) Framework): Under Clause 2.1, the Debt Service Ratio (DSR) is established as a core measure of applicant repayment affordability. Under Clause 2.2, the maximum permissible DSR ceiling is set at 60% where the applicant's verified gross monthly income is below RM 3,000. Under Clause 2.3, where the applicant's verified gross monthly income is RM 3,000 or greater, the maximum permissible DSR ceiling is capped at 70%. Under Clause 2.4, the projected DSR calculated immediately after factoring in the proposed monthly instalment or minimum payment of the requested facility is binding and must not breach these thresholds under any circumstances. Under Clause 2.5, total monthly debt commitments must encompass all existing credit facilities reported in CCRIS/CTOS alongside substantiated unrecorded non-bank financial liabilities.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Net Disposable Income (NDI) Requirements
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 3.0 (Net Disposable Income (NDI) Requirements): Under Clause 3.1, all approved credit applications must satisfy a mandatory minimum Net Disposable Income (NDI) floor of RM 1,500 calculated on a post-drawdown basis, after factoring in all statutory deductions, living expenses, and total debt service commitments when the requested facility is drawn in full. Under Clause 3.2, pursuant to Circular CIR-2025-014 dated 20 November 2025, an enhanced NDI floor of RM 2,000 post-drawdown is strictly binding where the applicant supports three (3) or more dependants. Credit applications failing to meet the applicable NDI threshold under Clause 3.1 or Clause 3.2 shall be rejected automatically without exception.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Credit Bureau and CTOS Scoring Assessment
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 4.0 (Credit Bureau and CTOS Scoring Assessment): Under Clause 4.1, a full credit bureau check comprising Bank Negara Malaysia's CCRIS and registered credit reporting agency (CTOS) data is mandatory for every applicant. Under Clause 4.2, applicants achieving a CTOS score of 700 and above are classified under the Prime Tier, qualifying for optimal risk-based pricing and automated processing channels. Under Clause 4.4, applicants possessing a CTOS score between 650 and 699 are assigned Standard Tier pricing and standard verification workflows. Under Clause 4.5, any application reflecting a CTOS score below 650 is barred from automated approval pathways and requires mandatory manual escalation to a Senior Underwriter for holistic risk appraisal.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Delinquency and Adverse Credit Records
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 5.0 (Delinquency and Adverse Credit Records): Under Clause 5.2, any active or un-discharged bankruptcy record, pending or ongoing legal action, winding-up order, or Agensi Kaunseling dan Pengurusan Kredit (AKPK) distress tag identified in CTOS or CCRIS shall result in an absolute and non-appealable decline. Under Clause 5.4, an application must be declined if any existing credit facility registered under the applicant's name reflects two or more months (2+ months) in arrears within the preceding 12-month window. Furthermore, applicants currently enrolled in an active AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP) are categorically not eligible for any new unsecured credit facility from the Company.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Credit Limit Assignment and Facility Parameters
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 6.0 (Credit Limit Assignment and Facility Parameters): Under Clause 6.1, for applicants with a verified gross monthly income below RM 5,000, the maximum allowable aggregate initial credit limit across unsecured facilities shall not exceed two times (2x) the gross monthly income. Under Clause 6.2, for applicants with a verified gross monthly income of RM 5,000 or greater, the maximum initial credit limit is capped at three times (3x) gross monthly income. Under Clause 6.3, card and financing terms must observe product rules: AEON Classic Visa carries an annual fee of RM 0; Gold Visa RM 150 (waived upon 12 swipes per annum); Platinum Visa RM 400 (waived upon RM 30,000 annual spend); credit card finance charges are tiered at 15% p.a. for prompt payers, 17% p.a. otherwise, and 18% p.a. for accounts with 2+ late payments in 12 months; Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq) rates span 6.88% to 14.88% p.a. flat for RM 3,000 to RM 150,000 over 12 to 84 months; Motorcycle HP-i permits up to 90% margin for 12 to 60 months; Auto HP-i permits up to 90% margin for up to 108 months. Under Clause 6.4, the approved limit must never be utilized as an input feature in any predictive underwriting scoring model.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Underwriting Authority and Customer Complaints Handling
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 7.0 (Underwriting Authority and Customer Complaints Handling): Under Clause 7.1, underwriting delegation of authority limits must be strictly adhered to by credit assessment officers, system administrators, and Senior Underwriters, precluding any unilateral override of hard policy caps. Under Clause 7.2, any customer dispute or complaint regarding an underwriting determination or fee assessment must be officially acknowledged within two (2) business days and definitively resolved within fourteen (14) calendar days. Unresolved complaints that cannot be reconciled internally within the stipulated timeframe must be escalated to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS) in accordance with regulatory governance guidelines.

title: Credit Underwriting Policy (v2)
heading: Model Governance, Validation, and Regulatory Compliance
chunk_text:
[POL-CR-001-v2 | Credit Underwriting Policy (v2) | v2.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause Section 8.0 (Model Governance, Validation, and Regulatory Compliance): Under Clause 8.1, all automated scorecards, algorithmic decision rules, and artificial intelligence models deployed within the credit underwriting pipeline must adhere to strict model governance protocols; specifically, the approved credit limit must never be an input feature to prevent circularity and target leakage. Under Clause 8.4, all credit underwriting models and business rules are subject to mandatory annual validation, independent internal audit review, and periodic stress-testing to guarantee continuous alignment with Bank Negara Malaysia guidelines on responsible financing.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Purpose and Scope
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 1.0 (Purpose and Scope): This Standard specifies the documentary requirements, validation mechanisms, and calculation rules for establishing the verified Gross Monthly Income of individual applicants. This standard applies to all retail credit applications submitted to AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad, including AEON Classic Visa, AEON Gold Visa, AEON Platinum Visa, Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq), Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i, Auto Hire Purchase-i, and Product (Objective) Financing. Establishing verified income is essential for applying Credit Policy v2 thresholds, including DSR caps (60% or 70%), NDI floors (RM 1,500 or RM 2,000), and credit limit multiplier caps (2x or 3x).

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Salaried Applicants Documentation Rules
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Salaried Applicants Documentation Rules): Salaried applicants are classified into confirmed permanent employees and contract staff. Permanent employees must submit their latest consecutive three (3) months' salary slips and latest consecutive three (3) months' bank statements reflecting salary crediting, or the latest EPF (KWSP) statement showing consecutive minimum six (6) months of employee and employer contributions. For contract employees, a minimum of consecutive six (6) months' payslips and bank statements are mandatory alongside an active employment contract with at least six (6) months remaining tenure.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Self-Employed and Business Owner Documentation Rules
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Self-Employed and Business Owner Documentation Rules): Self-employed individuals, sole proprietors, active partners, and majority company directors must provide business registration documents from the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM) reflecting at least twenty-four (24) months of active business operations. Applicants must submit the latest six (6) consecutive months of primary business operating bank account statements, together with the latest Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (LHDN) Form B/BE and formal tax payment receipts. Net business income is calculated using a standard operating margin haircut based on industry category or an audited average monthly profit.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Gig Economy and Variable Income Documentation Rules
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Gig Economy and Variable Income Documentation Rules): Gig economy workers, commission-based agents, and freelancers must provide consecutive six (6) months' commission statements or platform earning summary logs, accompanied by consecutive six (6) months of bank statements evidencing continuous inflows. A statutory 20% stability haircut is applied to the gross six-month rolling average to derive verified Gross Monthly Income. Cash earnings without verifiable bank statement credits or formalized platform settlement documentation are strictly ineligible for computation.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Bank Statement Verification Protocols
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Bank Statement Verification Protocols): Bank statements provided by applicants must clearly display the account holder's name matching the NRIC, account number, bank logo, and transaction dates. Underwriters and automated document capture pipelines must examine statements for salary transaction codes (e.g., SAL, PAY, GIRO) matching payslip net figures within a +/- 5% variance. Statements showing signs of manual alteration, irregular rounded bulk cash deposits, or continuous inward/outward round-tripping to inflate cash flow must be immediately escalated for comprehensive fraud screening.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: EPF Statement Validation Guidelines
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (EPF Statement Validation Guidelines): EPF statements downloaded directly from the official i-Akaun portal are accepted as an independent primary verification source. The gross monthly salary is derived by dividing the employee contribution amount by the applicable statutory EPF contribution rate (e.g., 11%). The contribution history must show consistent monthly remittances without gaps exceeding thirty (30) days within the preceding six (6) months. Voluntary self-contributions under i-Saraan or third-party voluntary top-ups shall not be treated as regular employment income.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Verification Triggers and Enhanced Due Diligence
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.0 (Verification Triggers and Enhanced Due Diligence): Manual verification and verbal employment confirmation via official corporate telephone landlines are triggered under any of the following circumstances: (a) CTOS credit score falling between 650 and 699, (b) variance exceeding 10% between declared income and documentary verification, (c) newly established employment tenure under six (6) months, (d) applicant supporting three (3) or more dependants to ensure compliance with the RM 2,000 NDI floor, or (e) requested initial limit exceeding RM 30,000. Any active legal action, bankruptcy, or AKPK flag in CTOS results in immediate absolute decline.

title: Income Verification Standard
heading: Audit Trail and Record Retention
chunk_text:
[STD-CR-002 | Income Verification Standard | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 8.0 (Audit Trail and Record Retention): All source documents, optical character recognition (OCR) parsing logs, verified gross income computations, and underwriter verification worksheets must be retained in the digital document repository for a minimum period of seven (7) years following facility maturity or termination. Approved credit limits must be archived separately and must never be utilized as an input feature for proprietary credit scoring or automated underwriting assessment models.

title: Revision of NDI floor for applicants with dependants
heading: Revision of NDI Thresholds
chunk_text:
[CIR-01 | Revision of NDI floor for applicants with dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-11-20 | Access: internal | Lang: en]

Under Credit Policy v2, Clause 3.1 maintains the baseline NDI floor at RM 1,500, but introduces Clause 3.2, which mandates an increased NDI floor of RM 2,000 where the applicant supports 3 or more dependants. NDI calculation must account for the projected net income minus total monthly statutory deductions and financing commitments after drawing down the approved facility.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Purpose and Background
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 1.0 (Purpose and Background): This Circular (CIR-02 / CIR-2025-016) provides binding underwriting guidelines for retail credit operations at AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad. Following Circular CIR-2025-014 issued on 2025-11-20, which introduced the revised Net Disposable Income (NDI) threshold under Credit Policy v2 clause 3.2, credit underwriting officers must verify and record the exact number of legal and financial dependants supported by the primary financing applicant prior to approving any retail financing facility.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Definition of Spouse Dependant
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Definition of Spouse Dependant): A spouse qualifies as an eligible dependant if legally married to the applicant under Malaysian law (or foreign equivalent registered with the National Registration Department) and currently earning no independent gross personal income. Non-working spouses include full-time homemakers and unemployed partners. If the spouse earns demonstrable independent income or holds salaried employment, the spouse shall not be counted as a financial dependant for the purposes of the NDI assessment.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Definition of Child Dependant
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Definition of Child Dependant): A biological, legally adopted, or formal foster child qualifies as a dependant if the child is either: (a) under eighteen (18) years of age; (b) between eighteen (18) and twenty-five (25) years of age and currently enrolled in full-time formal secondary or tertiary education (including certificate, diploma, or undergraduate degree studies); or (c) physically or mentally incapacitated regardless of age, certified by a registered medical practitioner. Gainfully employed children earning independent wages must not be included.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Definition of Parent and Senior Dependant
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Definition of Parent and Senior Dependant): An applicant's biological, step, or legally adoptive parent qualifies as a dependant where the parent resides with the applicant or receives primary financial maintenance from the applicant, provided the parent does not receive active employment income, commercial enterprise profit, or regular retirement annuity exceeding RM 1,000 per month. Both the applicant's own parents and parents-in-law may qualify subject to verified primary financial dependency.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Verification and Documentary Standards
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Verification and Documentary Standards): Underwriters must obtain and verify authentic documentary evidence before entering the verified dependant count into the credit origination engine. Accepted proofs include: marriage certificates or family card for spouses; birth certificates or formal adoption orders for minor children; active student registration cards or official university acceptance letters for full-time tertiary students; and medical certificates or statutory declarations for incapacitated dependants and supported elderly parents.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Interaction with NDI Floor and Credit Limits
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (Interaction with NDI Floor and Credit Limits): Where the verified dependant count is zero (0), one (1), or two (2), the mandatory NDI floor after the proposed facility is drawn in full is RM 1,500. Where the applicant supports three (3) or more verified dependants, Credit Policy v2 clause 3.2 strictly mandates an elevated NDI floor of RM 2,000. In all cases, projected Debt Service Ratio (DSR) caps (60% for gross monthly income below RM 3,000; 70% for RM 3,000 and above) and initial limit ceilings (up to 2x income below RM 5,000; up to 3x income at or above RM 5,000) remain concurrently binding.

title: Clarification on counting dependants
heading: Audit Trail and Misrepresentation Penalties
chunk_text:
[CIR-02 | Clarification on counting dependants | v1.0 | Effective: 2025-12-05 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.0 (Audit Trail and Misrepresentation Penalties): All customer declarations regarding dependant counts must be cross-checked during verbal confirmation calls and verified against available database records. Falsification, intentional omission of dependants to bypass the RM 2,000 NDI floor, or wrongful inflation of dependants constitutes credit non-compliance. Underwriters failing to secure mandatory documentary proof prior to facility sanction will be referred to Credit Risk Governance for procedural audit review.

Clause 1.0 (Purpose and Background): This Circular (CIR-2026-012 / CIR-06) serves as an operational reminder to all retail financing operations, credit operations, and branch customer service personnel regarding the standardized calculation of Ibra' (rebate) for customers undertaking early settlement of Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq). In compliance with Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Guidelines on Ibra' (Rebate) for Islamic Banking Products, AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad ('the Company') is committed to ensuring full transparency, Shariah compliance, and computational precision across all settlement quotation notices.

title: Early settlement rebate computation reminder
heading: Regulatory and Shariah Foundation of Ibra'
chunk_text:
[CIR-06 | Early settlement rebate computation reminder | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-06-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Regulatory and Shariah Foundation of Ibra'): Under the Shariah contract of Murabahah via Tawarruq arrangement adopted in the Company's Personal Financing-i facility, the sale price agreed at contract inception is fixed and legally binding. Ibra' refers to an act of releasing rights, where the Company grants a discretionary rebate to the customer on unearned contractual profit when the facility is settled prior to the contractual maturity date. Per BNM regulatory guidelines, granting Ibra' upon full early settlement or early redemption via refinancing is mandatory for licensed institutions and must reflect the unearned profit over the unexpired financing tenure.

title: Early settlement rebate computation reminder
heading: Applicability and Facility Parameters
chunk_text:
[CIR-06 | Early settlement rebate computation reminder | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-06-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Applicability and Facility Parameters): This circular applies to all active Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq) accounts. For reference, the product offers financing amounts ranging from RM 3,000 to RM 150,000 with tenures spanning 12 to 84 months, under flat profit rates ranging from 6.88% p.a. to 14.88% p.a. flat. Early settlement calculations must encompass the entire remaining principal and earned profit up to the designated settlement cut-off date, less the prescribed Ibra' sum.

title: Early settlement rebate computation reminder
heading: Standardized Ibra' Computation Formula
chunk_text:
[CIR-06 | Early settlement rebate computation reminder | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-06-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Standardized Ibra' Computation Formula): The net settlement sum payable by the customer shall be derived as follows: Settlement Amount = Outstanding Selling Price minus Ibra' plus Permitted Late Payment Charges (Ta'widh) minus Advance Instalments Held in Suspense. The Ibra' amount represents the total unearned contractual profit computed on the effective profit rate basis corresponding to the remaining unexpired financing tenure. Administrative charges or early settlement fees are strictly prohibited from being deducted against the rebate entitlement, ensuring full conformity with BNM consumer protection standards.

title: Early settlement rebate computation reminder
heading: Worked Example: Settlement at Month 24 of 60-Month Facility
chunk_text:
[CIR-06 | Early settlement rebate computation reminder | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-06-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Worked Example: Settlement at Month 24 of 60-Month Facility): Consider a Personal Financing-i facility with a principal amount of RM 50,000.00 approved at a flat profit rate of 8.00% p.a. over a 60-month tenure. Total contractual profit equals RM 20,000.00 (RM 50,000.00 x 8.00% x 5 years), yielding a Total Selling Price of RM 70,000.00 and an equated monthly instalment of RM 1,166.67. If the customer requests early settlement at Month 24 after servicing 24 prompt instalments (cumulative instalments paid: RM 28,000.08), the gross outstanding selling price is RM 41,999.92. Applying the reducing balance amortisation schedule mandated by BNM, the earned profit over the initial 24 months is RM 10,845.20, leaving an unearned profit of RM 9,154.80. Consequently, Ibra' granted is RM 9,154.80, and the net settlement amount due is RM 32,845.12.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: Purpose, Scope, and Regulatory Framework
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 1.0 (Purpose, Scope, and Regulatory Framework): This procedure governs the digital identity verification and customer onboarding workflows across all financing facilities offered by AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad ('the Company'), including AEON Classic Visa, Gold Visa, Platinum Visa, Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq), Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i, Auto Hire Purchase-i, and Product Financing. Operating in full compliance with the Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Policy Document on Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC), this SOP establishes mandatory controls for MyKad capture, biometric liveness detection, screening protocols, and manual fallback pathways.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: MyKad Document Capture and OCR Extraction
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (MyKad Document Capture and OCR Extraction): Applicants must upload high-resolution original colour images of the front and reverse of their Malaysian National Registration Identity Card (MyKad). The onboarding application executes optical character recognition (OCR) to extract the MyKad number, full legal name, residential address, date of birth, and gender. The automated engine performs document integrity checks, validating the presence of the security ghost portrait, micro-lettering, holographic features, and the internal algorithmic checksum of the identity card number. Blurred, cropped, black-and-white, or tampered images are automatically rejected.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: Facial Biometrics and Passive/Active Liveness Detection
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Facial Biometrics and Passive/Active Liveness Detection): Upon successful validation of the MyKad capture, the applicant must complete a real-time facial biometric scan via the mobile application or secure web interface. The system conducts an active liveness verification challenge (such as head rotation, blinking, or random expression prompts) alongside passive 3D depth analysis to detect presentation attacks, printed photographs, video replays, or synthetic deepfake masks. Extracted facial vectors are compared against the MyKad portrait photo. The automated verification requires a facial similarity match score of 85.0% or higher. Matches falling below 85.0% are blocked from straight-through processing.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: Sanctions, Politically Exposed Persons (PEP), and Adverse Media Screening
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Sanctions, Politically Exposed Persons (PEP), and Adverse Media Screening): Prior to credit evaluation, the core processing engine submits the applicant's verified full name and MyKad number against the United Nations Security Council Resolutions (UNSCR) consolidated sanctions list, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) domestic suppression register, Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) registries, and adverse media watchlists. Any exact match against targeted financial sanctions results in an immediate freeze of the digital session and automated notification to the Compliance AML/CFT Unit. Potential or partial PEP matches are flagged for Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and require Line Manager clearance before progressing.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: Credit Bureau Integration and Underwriting Pre-Filter
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Credit Bureau Integration and Underwriting Pre-Filter): Following successful identity validation and negative screening clearance, the platform calls external credit bureau services including CTOS Data Systems and CCRIS. In line with Credit Policy v2, credit scores are categorized immediately: scores of 700 and above are allocated to the prime tier, scores between 650 and 699 are assigned standard risk-based pricing, and scores below 650 are disqualified from the automated processing pipeline and queued for Senior Underwriter review. If the bureau report indicates active bankruptcy, pending legal action, an active AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP) flag, or any existing credit facility currently 2 or more months in arrears, the system executes an absolute decline without exception.

title: eKYC Onboarding Procedure
heading: Manual Fallback and Exception Handling Protocol
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-001 | eKYC Onboarding Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (Manual Fallback and Exception Handling Protocol): Applicants failing automated eKYC due to camera resolution limitations, minor document glare, OCR character ambiguity, or marginal biometric match scores between 70.0% and 84.9% are diverted into the manual fallback workflow. A specialized Operations Verification Officer examines the uncompressed digital assets, cross-checks National Registration Department (JPN) verification databases where integrated, and may initiate an authenticated outbound video verification call. The applicant is granted up to three automated capture attempts before manual diversion occurs. If manual verification cannot decisively confirm identity within 2 business days, the application is cancelled.

Operations staff must log all formal complaints immediately, issue an official written acknowledgment to the applicant within 2 business days, and provide a full resolution within 14 calendar days. If a dispute regarding identity verification failure or credit declination cannot be resolved internally within 14 days, the customer must be formally advised of their right to escalate the matter to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS).

Document images and verification session logs must be retained securely for a statutory minimum of 7 years following customer onboarding or account closure. Under no circumstances may raw facial biometric images be exposed via unauthenticated endpoints or exported to unencrypted portable storage media.

Front-line customer service personnel, card operations specialists, and dispute investigation officers must adhere to the timelines and criteria stipulated in this document.

title: Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback
heading: Dispute Intake, Verification, and Acknowledgement
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-002 | Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Dispute Intake, Verification, and Acknowledgement): Cardholders must lodge a formal transaction dispute within sixty (60) calendar days from the date of the card statement on which the disputed transaction first appeared. Disputed claims must be submitted using the prescribed Cardholder Dispute Declaration Form accompanied by supporting evidence, including sales receipts, merchant correspondence, or police reports where unauthorised transactions or fraud are alleged. In compliance with the Company's customer service charter, all dispute notifications and complaints received must be formally acknowledged within two (2) business days from receipt.

title: Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback

chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-002 | Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Provisional Credit Assessment and Posting): Upon receipt of a substantiated dispute, the Card Operations team evaluates eligibility for provisional credit. For valid non-fraud processing errors (such as duplicate charges) and unauthorised card-not-present fraud, provisional credit equal to the disputed principal amount shall be credited to the cardholder account within seven (7) business days. Provisional credit is conditional: should the dispute be resolved in the merchant's favour following representment, or if the cardholder is determined to have acted with gross negligence, the provisional credit shall be reversed immediately with notice to the cardholder.

title: Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback

chunk_text:

Clause 4.0 (Visa Chargeback Processing and Reason Codes): All chargebacks must be lodged via the Visa Resolve Online (VROL) network in accordance with the latest Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules. Dispute specialists must categorise claims under one of the four principal Visa dispute families: Fraud (Family 10), Authorisation (Family 11), Processing Errors (Family 12), or Customer Disputes (Family 13). Specialists must ensure that all required narrative documentation, cardholder certifications, and digital audit trails satisfy Visa scheme requirements prior to electronic transmission within the scheme-mandated timeframes.

title: Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback

chunk_text:

Clause 5.0 (Representment, Pre-Arbitration, and Arbitration Workflows): When an acquirer submits a representment refuting a chargeback, the Card Operations unit has thirty (30) calendar days from the representment date to review the merchant's rebuttal documentation. If the merchant's proof fails to substantiate the charge, the officer shall file a Pre-Arbitration case via VROL within thirty (30) days. If the pre-arbitration is declined by the acquirer and the dispute merit exceeds standard cost-recovery thresholds, the dispute may be escalated to formal Visa Arbitration upon approval by the Head of Card Operations.

title: Card Transaction Dispute and Chargeback

In complex scenarios requiring prolonged international merchant trace, an interim status update must be provided on day 14. If a dispute or complaint cannot be resolved satisfactorily within the internal framework, the cardholder shall be formally advised of their right to escalate the matter to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS) within six (6) months of the Company's final decision letter.

If card annual fees (RM 150 for Gold or RM 400 for Platinum) or promotional fee waivers were compromised as an operational consequence of an unresolved dispute, the Operations team shall effect appropriate manual billing corrections.

The settlement quotation shall strictly possess a validity period of 7 calendar days from the date of generation. If full settlement funds are not credited within this 7-day validity window, the quotation lapses automatically and a revised settlement quotation reflecting recalculated unearned profit and accrued charges must be generated.

title: Early Settlement Processing
heading: Rebate (Ibra') Computation Methodology
chunk_text:

Clause 3.0 (Rebate (Ibra') Computation Methodology): In compliance with Shariah governance requirements and statutory guidelines, the Company grants a rebate (ibra') on unearned profit to customers who settle their Islamic financing facilities prior to maturity. The net early settlement figure is calculated as the outstanding sale price minus unearned profit (calculated via Rule of 78 or reducing balance amortisation schedule as specified in product terms) minus statutory rebate adjustments, plus any overdue instalments, late payment compensation (ta'widh) accrued to date, and administrative discharge fees if applicable.

title: Early Settlement Processing

Operations must perform same-day reconciliation upon credit advice. Where payment is made by cheque or bank draft, the early settlement is considered provisional pending clearance. No facility account closure or collateral release may occur until funds have irrevocably cleared into the Company's operational disbursement account.

For secured facilities such as Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i (tenure 12 to 60 months) and Auto Hire Purchase-i (tenure up to 108 months), the Collateral Management Unit shall execute vehicle e-Hakmilik cancellation in the JPJ (Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan) database and release the physical vehicle registration card or digital clearance confirmation to the hirer.

chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 1.0 (Purpose and Operational Scope): This procedure outlines the operational steps for evaluating permanent credit limit increase applications for existing credit cardholders holding AEON Classic Visa, AEON Gold Visa, and AEON Platinum Visa accounts, as well as revolving credit line facilities administered by AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad. All operations personnel and underwriting staff must adhere strictly to these processing standards to maintain prudential credit quality and regulatory compliance.

title: Credit Limit Increase Review
heading: Mandatory Account Seasoning Rule
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Mandatory Account Seasoning Rule): No credit limit increase shall be granted within the first 12 months of facility opening under any circumstances. The credit card or revolving credit account must have completed a minimum of 12 full billing cycles with an active, uninterrupted payment history. Any customer request or system-generated trigger initiated prior to the 12-month tenure threshold must be systematically rejected by the loan origination system without manual override.

title: Credit Limit Increase Review
heading: Income Eligibility and Multiplier Limits
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Income Eligibility and Multiplier Limits): Credit limit increases are subject to statutory income multiplier limits based on verified gross monthly income. For cardholders with gross monthly income below RM 3,000, the maximum aggregate credit limit shall not exceed 2 times gross monthly income. For gross monthly income between RM 3,000 and RM 4,999, the revised limit remains capped at 2 times gross monthly income. For cardholders with verified gross monthly income of RM 5,000 and above, the approved limit may be increased up to a maximum cap of 3 times gross monthly income. In accordance with policy governance, an approved credit limit must never be utilized as a machine learning model input.

title: Credit Limit Increase Review
heading: Affordability Criteria: DSR and NDI Compliance
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Affordability Criteria: DSR and NDI Compliance): All limit increase reviews require re-calculation of the applicant's affordability metrics. The projected Debt Service Ratio (DSR) including the revised credit limit commitments must not exceed 60% for applicants earning gross monthly income under RM 3,000, or 70% for applicants earning RM 3,000 and above. Additionally, the applicant must satisfy the binding Net Disposable Income (NDI) floor post-facility calculation: a minimum NDI floor of RM 1,500 applies where the applicant supports fewer than 3 dependants, and a raised NDI floor of RM 2,000 applies where the applicant supports 3 or more dependants.

title: Credit Limit Increase Review
heading: Credit Bureau Assessment and Disqualifying Flags
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Credit Bureau Assessment and Disqualifying Flags): A fresh CTOS credit bureau assessment is mandatory for all credit limit increase requests. Applicants with a CTOS score of 700 or above qualify for prime tier automated evaluation; scores between 650 and 699 require standard manual underwriting review; and scores below 650 must not pass via automated pathways and mandate Senior Underwriter review. An immediate absolute decline must be executed if the CTOS report indicates pending legal action, active bankruptcy status, or an AKPK flag. Furthermore, any applicant with an existing internal or external credit facility currently 2 or more months in arrears, or enrolled in an active AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP), is strictly ineligible for a credit limit increase.

title: Credit Limit Increase Review
heading: Customer Consent and Verification Standards
chunk_text:
[SOP-OPS-005 | Credit Limit Increase Review | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (Customer Consent and Verification Standards): In strict compliance with regulatory guidelines, AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad strictly prohibits unilateral or unsolicited credit limit increases. Every limit increase requires affirmative, documented customer consent obtained via signed physical variation form, verified two-factor digital banking consent, or recorded telephone interaction on a compliant voice line. Underwriters must verify customer identity and obtain current income documentation, defined as the latest 3 months salary slips, latest EPF contribution statement, or 6 months bank statements for self-employed individuals.

For rejected requests, a formal adverse notification letter or electronic advice detailing general criteria must be dispatched. In the event of customer complaints regarding limit increase decisions, customer care representatives must formally acknowledge the complaint within 2 business days and resolve the dispute within 14 calendar days. Unresolved complaints must be escalated to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS).

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Purpose and Governance Framework
chunk_text:

Clause 1.0 (Purpose and Governance Framework): This Collections Strategy document sets out the operational procedures, communication governance, and recovery workflows across successive delinquency buckets for AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad ('the Company'). It applies across all consumer financing products, including AEON Classic Visa, AEON Gold Visa, and AEON Platinum Visa credit cards, Personal Financing-i (Tawarruq), Motorcycle Hire Purchase-i, Auto Hire Purchase-i, and Product (Objective) Financing. All debt recovery practices must adhere strictly to Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Guidelines on Fair Debt Collection Practices, relevant consumer credit legislation, and internal credit policies.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Bucket 1: Early Arrears (1 to 30 Days Past Due)
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Bucket 1: Early Arrears (1 to 30 Days Past Due)): Bucket 1 focuses on automated, low-friction payment reminders aimed at curing administrative oversights and short-term cash flow misalignments. Communication channels include automated Short Message Service (SMS), WhatsApp business messaging, email notifications, and automated interactive voice responses. Outreach is capped at a maximum of two contact attempts per week. Accounts rolling past the payment due date lose any applicable 15% per annum prompt-payer finance charge tier on credit cards and revert to the standard 17% per annum rate.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Bucket 2: Mid Arrears (31 to 60 Days Past Due)
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Bucket 2: Mid Arrears (31 to 60 Days Past Due)): Accounts entering Bucket 2 are routed to internal outbound tele-collection officers to determine root causes of non-payment and secure binding Promises to Pay (PTP). Outbound calls are permitted up to three attempts per week between 08:30 and 19:00 hours on working days. Unsecured credit facilities, including credit card lines and revolving facilities, are subjected to temporary charging suspensions. Officers are empowered to offer short-term instalment arrangements where temporary cash impairment is verified.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Bucket 3: Serious Arrears (61 to 90 Days Past Due)
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Bucket 3: Serious Arrears (61 to 90 Days Past Due)): Bucket 3 triggers intensified recovery actions and formal regulatory notifications. Under internal credit policy, any customer with a facility currently two or more months in arrears is classified as an immediate systemic decline for any new financing applications. Credit card accounts with two or more late payments over the preceding 12 months are escalated to the maximum finance charge of 18% per annum. For Motorcycle and Auto Hire Purchase-i accounts, statutory notices under the Fourth Schedule of the Hire-Purchase Act 1967 (Notice of Intention to Repossess) are generated upon reaching the statutory default threshold. Total outbound contact attempts shall not exceed four attempts per week, complemented by field visits where telecommunication contact fails.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Bucket 4: Pre-Default and Repossession (91 to 180 Days Past Due)
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (Bucket 4: Pre-Default and Repossession (91 to 180 Days Past Due)): Accounts exceeding 90 Days Past Due are classified as impaired (Stage 3) under Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) 9. Facilities are assigned to specialized recovery teams or outsourced to panel legal firms for issuance of formal Letters of Demand (LOD). For Auto HP-i and Motorcycle HP-i agreements, physical repossession orders are executed by registered repossession agents in strict compliance with statutory guidelines. Contact frequency is maintained at up to three structured touchpoints per week. Customers demonstrating distress may be guided to the Agensi Kaunseling dan Pengurusan Kredit (AKPK) for Debt Management Programme (DMP) intervention prior to litigation.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Bucket 5: Write-Off Thresholds and Post-Write-Off Recovery (181+ Days Past Due)
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (Bucket 5: Write-Off Thresholds and Post-Write-Off Recovery (181+ Days Past Due)): Facilities reaching 180 Days Past Due without an active repayment plan or formalized rescheduling agreement are automatically reviewed for accounting charge-off and write-off. Write-off does not extinguish the legal debt. Post-write-off recovery includes engagement of vetted external Debt Collection Agencies (DCAs), legal summons, Judgment Debtor Summons (JDS), and initiation of bankruptcy proceedings where total unsecured indebtedness fulfills legal thresholds. An active AKPK flag, bankruptcy petition, or legal judgment results in permanent negative CTOS indicators and absolute decline for any future financing with the Company.

title: Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket
heading: Debt Relief and Restructuring Protocols
chunk_text:
[COL-001 | Collections Strategy by Arrears Bucket | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.0 (Debt Relief and Restructuring Protocols): Borrowers experiencing persistent financial distress may request facility restructuring or enroll into an AKPK Debt Management Programme (DMP). Upon formal notification of DMP participation from AKPK, all direct collection communications, legal enforcement, and repossession procedures are stayed immediately. Customers with an active AKPK DMP remain ineligible for any new unsecured credit facilities with the Company. It applies to all onboarding channels and lifecycle monitoring for retail financing facilities, credit card products (Classic, Gold, Platinum Visa), and Islamic hire purchase arrangements. chunk_text:

Clause 2.0 (Standard Customer Due Diligence (CDD)): Customer Due Diligence must be executed prior to onboarding, credit facility activation, or card issuance. Verification for individual Malaysian citizens requires visual and cryptographic inspection of the original MyKad alongside automated biometric facial match or MyKad chip fingerprint verification. Residential address, source of wealth, and ongoing employment must be verified using utility bills, official salary slips, or statutory EPF statements. Non-individual entities must undergo full corporate profiling, establishing legal registration, business operations, and the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) holding 25% or more equity interest.

title: AML/CFT and Targeted Financial Sanctions Procedure
heading: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Triggers
chunk_text:
[CMP-001 | AML/CFT and Targeted Financial Sanctions Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Triggers): Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatorily triggered where an applicant: (a) is identified as a foreign or domestic Politically Exposed Person (PEP), or an immediate family member or close associate thereof; (b) originates from or maintains financial exposure connected to high-risk jurisdictions identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF); (c) applies for individual financing aggregating RM 100,000 or above without standard formal payroll documentation; or (d) exhibits adverse media indicators related to financial crime, fraud, or predicate offences. EDD entails obtaining documented Senior Management approval, establishing verifiable source of wealth, and conducting intensified transaction surveillance.

title: AML/CFT and Targeted Financial Sanctions Procedure

chunk_text:

Clause 4.0 (Targeted Financial Sanctions (TFS) Screening): Real-time automated sanctions screening must be performed against all applicants, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners prior to entering into any commercial relationship. Screening lists incorporate the United Nations Security Council Resolutions (UNSCR) consolidated sanctions database and domestic lists gazetted by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MOHA) under the relevant United Nations sanctions implementation regulations. If a confirmed match is identified, the application must be declined immediately without tipping off the applicant, funds or accounts frozen without delay, and an immediate statutory report lodged with the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department (FIED) of BNM.

The Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) shall investigate the report independently. Where reasonable grounds for suspicion exist, the MLRO must file a formal Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with BNM FIED via the online FIIMS portal within the prescribed statutory deadline. Strict anti-tipping-off provisions apply under Section 14A of AMLA; staff must not disclose STR deliberations to the customer or any unauthorized party.

Customer risk ratings must be reviewed periodically: Low Risk profiles every 36 months, Medium Risk profiles every 24 months, and High Risk profiles at least annually. In accordance with AMLA statutory retention mandates, all CDD records, facility application files, transaction slips, and STR documentation must be securely retained for a minimum of seven (7) years following account termination or transaction execution.

title: Personal Data Protection Handling Procedure
heading: Core Personal Data Protection Principles
chunk_text:
[CMP-002 | Personal Data Protection Handling Procedure | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Core Personal Data Protection Principles): The Company mandates adherence to the seven key PDPA principles across all customer touchpoints: (1) General Principle: personal data must only be processed with explicit, informed consent for lawful purposes; (2) Notice and Choice Principle: data subjects must be informed via written Privacy Notices of data collection purposes and rights; (3) Disclosure Principle: personal data must not be disclosed to unapproved third parties without explicit consent; (4) Security Principle: robust technological, administrative, and physical safeguards must protect against loss, misuse, or unauthorized modification; (5) Retention Principle: data must not be kept longer than necessary for the fulfillment of financing agreements or legal requirements; (6) Data Integrity Principle: all reasonable steps must ensure customer data is accurate, complete, and updated; and (7) Access Principle: customers retain the statutory right to request access to and correction of their personal records.

Customer service personnel must verify the applicant's identity using primary identification (MyKad or passport) prior to registering the request in the central compliance tracking system. Requests regarding credit facility assessments, repayment histories, or account statements must be validated against core customer databases without altering historical transaction trails.

If fulfillment cannot be completed within the initial 21-day window due to multi-system data aggregation, archival retrieval, or system unavailability, an extension not exceeding an additional fourteen (14) calendar days may be invoked. In such instances, a formal Notification of Extension (Form PDPA-EXT-01) stating substantive reasons must be issued to the data subject prior to the expiration of the original 21-day timeline.

The Incident Response Team must contain the exposure, conduct an impact triage within twenty-four (24) hours, and determine regulatory reporting obligations to the Personal Data Protection Commissioner (PDP) and relevant financial authorities.

All frontline personnel, credit underwriters, customer service officers, and collection agents are mandated to detect, freeze, and report suspicious activities in strict adherence to Bank Negara Malaysia guidelines and internal risk governance standards.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: Application Fraud and Identity Theft
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 2.0 (Application Fraud and Identity Theft): Application fraud involves the submission of fabricated, altered, or stolen applicant credentials to procure credit facilities deceptively. Typical red flags include tampered salary slips, forged Employees Provident Fund (EPF) statements, inconsistent employer telephone numbers, mismatched MyKad microprint data, and non-operational corporate addresses. Assessors must verify whether CTOS identity records indicate deceased individual identifiers or duplicate employer contact details shared across unrelated applicant profiles. Any application displaying manipulated income documentation to deliberately circumvent Debt Service Ratio (DSR) ceilings (60% for income below RM 3,000; 70% for RM 3,000 and above) or Net Disposable Income (NDI) floors (RM 1,500 standard; RM 2,000 for applicants supporting three or more dependants) shall be declined and escalated immediately.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: Mule Accounts and Disbursement Redirection
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 3.0 (Mule Accounts and Disbursement Redirection): Money mule typologies involve recruiting vulnerable or complicit individuals who surrender control of their bank accounts or identity documents to criminal syndicates. In retail financing, red flags include third-party disbursement requests, rapid bank account detail amendments submitted immediately prior to contract execution, or salary crediting histories showing circular peer-to-peer transfers rather than authenticated corporate payroll. For Personal Financing-i disbursements ranging from RM 3,000 to RM 150,000, underwriter match validation between the primary applicant identity and the target disbursement account is mandatory; unverified third-party account nominations result in immediate suspension of facility disbursement.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: Account Takeover (ATO) and Credential Compromise
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 4.0 (Account Takeover (ATO) and Credential Compromise): Account Takeover occurs when unauthorized third parties gain control of authentic customer profiles through credential harvesting, SIM swapping, phishing campaigns, or social engineering. Prominent indicators include sudden requests to update registered mobile numbers or mailing addresses without accompanying certified MyKad validation, followed immediately by card reissuance requests, password resets, or cash advance drawdowns on credit card products. Automated fraud monitoring systems must halt online transacting and notify the legitimate customer whenever high-velocity, off-hour transactions originate from foreign IP addresses or unregistered mobile devices.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: First-Party Fraud and Bust-Out Schemes
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 5.0 (First-Party Fraud and Bust-Out Schemes): First-party fraud involves individuals who secure credit facilities with zero genuine intention of repayment. In 'bust-out' schemes, applicants maintain a pristine repayment history for initial tenures to secure progressive credit limit increases (up to the maximum 2x monthly income for earnings below RM 5,000 or 3x for earnings of RM 5,000 and above), followed by sudden 100% line utilisation across cash-convertible merchant categories, complete default, and abandonment of all contact channels. In financing facilities such as Personal Financing-i or Product Financing, the total absence of the first scheduled instalment (First Payment Default) constitutes a severe primary red flag requiring immediate field visitation and debt recovery enforcement.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: Dealer, Merchant, and Point-of-Sale Collusion
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 6.0 (Dealer, Merchant, and Point-of-Sale Collusion): Collusive fraud involves external motorcycle or automotive dealers acting in concert with applicants or rogue sales agents to exploit Hire Purchase-i financing. Major typologies include phantom vehicle financing (advancing funds against non-existent vehicle chassis numbers), artificial invoice inflation to bypass the maximum 90% margin of financing, and double-pledging the same asset across multiple financial institutions. Field inspectors must execute physical pre-disbursement verification of vehicle identification numbers (VIN), engine numbers, and registration card records with Road Transport Department (JPJ) registers prior to any capital disbursement.

title: Fraud Typologies and Red Flags
heading: Investigation, Escalation, and Incident Management
chunk_text:
[CMP-004 | Fraud Typologies and Red Flags | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: internal | Lang: en]
Clause 7.0 (Investigation, Escalation, and Incident Management): Upon identifying suspected fraudulent behaviour, operational units must lodge a Fraud Incident Notification with the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) within four operating hours. If an incident stems from a customer dispute, customer care representatives must acknowledge receipt within two business days and resolve the investigation within fourteen calendar days. Where customers remain dissatisfied with unresolved outcomes regarding fraud liability, cases must be systematically referred to the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS). Where confirmed criminal activity or systemic mule ring activity is identified, SIU shall file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with the Financial Intelligence and Enforcement Department of Bank Negara Malaysia and lodge an official police report.

Clause Q1 (What is Personal Financing-i and what Shariah concept does it follow?): Personal Financing-i is an unsecured Islamic personal financing facility offered by AEON Credit Service (M) Berhad ("the Company") based on the Shariah principle of Murabahah via Tawarruq (commodity sale and purchase arrangement). Under this concept, the customer purchases a specific Shariah-compliant commodity from the Company at a cost-plus-profit sale price on deferred payment terms and appoints the Company as an agent to sell the commodity on their behalf to a third-party trader to obtain liquid cash funds.

The minimum gross monthly income requirement is evaluated against the Company's credit framework, ensuring compliance with Net Disposable Income (NDI) and Debt Service Ratio (DSR) ceilings.

title: Personal Financing-i FAQ

chunk_text:

Clause Q12 (How can I settle my financing early, and how is Ibra' (rebate) calculated?): Customers may execute full early settlement by giving written notice to the Company. In accordance with Bank Negara Malaysia Shariah guidelines, the Company grants Ibra' (rebate) on the unearned contracted profit. The early settlement amount is calculated as: Settlement Amount = Outstanding Selling Price minus Ibra' (Unearned Profit) plus any Undue Late Payment Charges. Ibra' is computed using the standard actuarial rule of 78 or reducing balance formula.

title: Personal Financing-i FAQ

Auto Hire Purchase-i offers financing tenures ranging from 12 months up to a maximum of 108 months, subject to vehicle age, model, and credit assessment.

chunk_text:
[FAQ-HP-EN | Motorcycle and Auto Hire Purchase-i FAQ | v1.0 | Effective: 2026-01-01 | Access: public | Lang: en]

A CTOS score of 700 and above qualifies for the prime pricing tier, while scores between 650 and 699 are eligible under standard pricing terms. Applications with a CTOS score below 650 cannot proceed via the automated straight-through approval path and require manual review by a Senior Underwriter. Any record of bankruptcy, active legal action, or adverse AKPK flagging results in an absolute decline.

Clause 2.0 (Definition of Qualifying Dependants): For credit assessment purposes under Credit Policy v2, a qualifying dependant is defined as an individual who relies wholly or substantially on the applicant for financial maintenance. This includes: (a) a legal spouse not in receipt of independent regular income, (b) biological, legally adopted, or step-children under the age of 18, or under 24 if enrolled in full-time tertiary education, and (c) biological or legally adoptive parents or parents-in-law aged 60 and above with no independent pension or recurring income.
